Spanish PM Pedro Sánchez:
This illegal war in the Middle East and the tensions in the Strait of Hormuz illustrate, I believe, the price Europe has to pay, and indeed the rest of the world, particularly the Global South.
So far this year, this war has cost Europeans an additional €100 billion because of rising fuel prices.

Spanish PM Pedro Sánchez:
There are books that tell the story of a life, and there are books that mark the end of an era. I believe Stefan Zweig's The World of Yesterday does both.
In its first half, this great writer describes his childhood and youth in a Europe that was cosmopolitan, where friendships crossed borders.
A Europe confident in itself, convinced that interdependence between nations and societies was the best antidote to armed conflict.
The second part, however, tells how nationalism and ancient hatreds destroyed that world, destroying bonds and certainties that seemed solid but ultimately proved not to be.

Spanish PM Pedro Sánchez:
Spain has demonstrated, with facts, that it is possible to grow, create jobs, and at the same time reduce the public deficit and public debt without cutting or sacrificing public policies.

Spanish PM Pedro Sánchez:
When everything breaks down, what holds us together is what belongs to all of us: a public healthcare system, public emergency services, public security forces, and public servants who are always there to serve the people.

Spanish PM Pedro Sánchez:
There are countries that do not want to leave Europe, but rather want to join it.
This means that our European project, the European Union, is not in decline. Quite the opposite.
It is a moral beacon for humanity, a lifeline for human rights, democracy, social and territorial cohesion, and progress.

♦️

We are not going to destroy this or that country.
In fact, many of these countries, former colonial powers, are falling apart on their own.
More and more of the people they enslaved and colonized are waking up and rising up.
They are gaining and reviving their self-awareness and self-determination.
All their politics is built on confrontation. They constantly need an enemy.

On the other side, we also have contacts with Russia's Foreign Ministry and the Presidential Administration, and of course, on both sides, with their affiliated intelligence services.
We are well connected. We are treated as equals.
